description: The >>CALL-CONVENTION {COBOL | convention-name} compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.9) - it associates a convention-name with a set of implementor-defined call conventions for CALL/INVOKE and the ENTRY convention. Recognized and consumed by the text-manipulation stage; WiseOwl COBOL defines no call-convention-name, so >>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL is the only accepted form and its no-op disposition is faithful (any other word is COBOL1911, kb/Work PB1383); the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.8: 'The CALL-CONVENTION directive instructs the compiler how to treat references to program-names and method-names'; §2002:7.2.8.2 GR1: 'The default for the CALL-CONVENTION directive is >>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL' (item 29's list does not name CALL-CONVENTION by itself; the 2002 clause is the authority). 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.8: 'The CALL-CONVENTION directive instructs the compiler how to treat references to program-names') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.9.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.9.2 general format: { COBOL | call-convention-name-1 }, plain braces — exactly one shall be written; call-convention-name-1 names one of the implementor's call conventions (§2023:7.3.9.3 GR2b maps program-names under it 'in a manner defined by the implementor'), and WiseOwl COBOL defines none, so COBOL is the whole admissible set and any other word names no convention.

source:
>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725CC.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
